prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 31 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

source_trace.value: The result is preregistered and reproducible but remains an OPEN reconstructed-mirror archive test pending deterministic source validation and does not provide a complete population denominator.
These are blind narrative screen counts, not manually adjudicated physical identities and not mutually exclusive categories.
Mirror presentation-layer disposition labels are rejected from inference. The matched control uses occurrence date plus narrative morphology and does not use disposition_screen.
Narrative Summary only; fixed record-card checkbox vocabulary excluded by v0.2 corrective runner.
This preregistered exact-date archive test likewise shows no positive STARLIKE or all-case enrichment at +/-1 against either blocked null.
Previously did not reproduce the reported positive +/-1-day nuclear enhancement or positive day+1 enhancement.

The open data support a nonzero baseline of photographic candidates and human-reported star-like/compact-light anomalies outside nuclear-test windows. Nuclear temporal proximity is not a specific discriminator by itself.

A high-reporting human anomaly epoch with star-like and compact-light morphology exists in a month containing no strict-calendar nuclear-test dates, directly demonstrating a substantial non-nuclear human-report baseline.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large central circle of observers in active discussion, surrounded by independent groups on several levels. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: an elder teaches a younger apprentice on a side stair; a witness group debates and compares observations under a small arch; workers and artisans cooperate in a lower corner; travelers and families cross a distant bridge while messengers move between levels. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 34 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 34 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 31 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

Around it place about 31 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 34 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

The public control reconstruction demonstrates that number of nuclear-test event rows and number of unique nuclear-test calendar dates are different quantities. Strict has 124 event rows but 121 unique dates; broad has 126 event rows but 123 unique dates. This may explain part of historical 124/125/126 ambiguity but does not prove byte/row equivalence to the unrecovered Bruehl-Villarroel calendar.

The primary +/-1 null remains strongly compatible with schedule-preserving permutations. The wider negative parametric signals are materially attenuated; only strict +/-4 crosses 0.05 in this simple post-hoc blocked diagnostic, while broad +/-4 does not. This is not sufficient evidence for nuclear suppression.

prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them; enlarge this human-led central subject and make faces, gestures and interaction unmistakable before any architecture is noticed. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 31 additional human figures in at least 8 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

source_trace.value: This is a strong independent open transport result, but it is not byte-equivalent to the closed original catalog and longer-window structure still requires sky-position/artifact controls.
This is a processed tile-time denominator, not yet exact non-overlapping geometric deg2-minute sky exposure.
Bruehl-Villarroel reported a positive nuclear-window association in their closed analysis sample and a large day-after comparison.
This result does not prove that every row in the closed 107,875-source catalog is artifactual and does not constitute byte-exact refutation of that unavailable sample.
The sign and significance of the reported positive +/-1 association do not transport into this independently selected, fully public POSS-I cohort.

This open result is qualitatively consistent with reanalyses that find observation/exposure normalization weakens the positive association, but non-equivalent catalogs and calendar definitions prevent treating them as one pooled replication.

Add plate/tile sky-position controls before interpreting longer-window negative structure. Observation date selects which right ascensions/fields were photographed; candidate density may vary with Galactic latitude, stellar density and catalog completeness.
Replace processed tile-minute proxy with exact non-overlapping valid WCS footprint area-time exposure.
Stratify by plate/copy/scanner/WCS quality and repaired-astrometry lineage where public metadata permit.
Add Kp/Ap, lunar and weather/visibility covariates from open sources with explicit missingness and provenance.
Freeze an event-time/lag design before reusing the exact-lag pattern as a confirmatory test.
Strict definition plus CRATER; UW excluded.

The public control reconstruction demonstrates that number of nuclear-test event rows and number of unique nuclear-test calendar dates are different quantities. Strict has 124 event rows but 121 unique dates; broad has 126 event rows but 123 unique dates. This may explain part of historical 124/125/126 ambiguity but does not prove byte/row equivalence to the unrecovered Bruehl-Villarroel calendar.
USA/USSR/UK AIRDROP/TOWER/SURFACE/ATMOSPH/BARGE/BALLOON/ROCKET/SHIP in the study window; CRATER and UW excluded.
The public cohort does not reproduce a positive day-after-test enhancement. Both frozen open calendars yield a modest negative point estimate whose confidence interval includes 1.

Significant negative point estimates several days BEFORE test dates are incompatible with a simple forward causal suppression story and instead flag temporal scheduling, observed-field composition or other confounding as mandatory targets.
Exact lag and blocked-permutation diagnostics were specified after inspection of the open primary +/-1 result and may not be treated as confirmatory discovery tests.

The primary +/-1 null remains strongly compatible with schedule-preserving permutations. The wider negative parametric signals are materially attenuated; only strict +/-4 crosses 0.05 in this simple post-hoc blocked diagnostic, while broad +/-4 does not. This is not sufficient evidence for nuclear suppression.

Negative Binomial NB2 with estimated dispersion, observation-date clustered covariance, log exposure_tile_min exposure, year_centered plus annual sine/cosine temporal covariates; Poisson retained as sensitivity.

Record the first fully public JANUS test of the reported POSS-I/nuclear-test association after removing dependence on the request-only 107,875-source VASCO catalog. The result tests transport of the association into an independently constructed, hash-pinned public cohort; it is not an exact replication of the closed sample.
JANUS POSS-I — Public-Only Nuclear-Association Reconstruction Result
